title: Henselization of pairs commutes with filtered colimits
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a directed set and $(A_\lambda,I_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ a directed system of pairs: commutative rings $A_\lambda$ with ideals $I_\lambda$ and ring maps $\varphi_{\mu\lambda}:A_\mu\to A_\lambda$ for $\mu\le\lambda$ (compatible, $\varphi_{\lambda\lambda}=\mathrm{id}$) with $\varphi_{\mu\lambda}(I_\mu)\subseteq I_\lambda$. Let $A=\varinjlim_\lambda A_\lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] with coprojections $\alpha_\lambda:A_\lambda\to A$, and let $I=\bigcup_\lambda\alpha_\lambda(I_\lambda)$ (an ideal of $A$, the colimit of the $I_\lambda$). For every $\lambda$ let $(A_\lambda^h,I_\lambda^h)$, $I_\lambda^h=I_\lambda A_\lambda^h$, be the henselization of $(A_\lambda,I_\lambda)$ [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization]. Then: (1) for $\mu\le\lambda$ there is exactly one ring map $\varphi^h_{\mu\lambda}:A_\mu^h\to A_\lambda^h$ with $\varphi^h_{\mu\lambda}\circ(A_\mu\to A_\mu^h)=(A_\lambda\to A_\lambda^h)\circ\varphi_{\mu\lambda}$, so that $(A^h_\lambda,I^h_\lambda)$ is a directed system of pairs; (2) let $A^h_\infty=\varinjlim_\lambda A^h_\lambda$ (colimit of rings along the $\varphi^h_{\mu\lambda}$) with coprojections $\iota_\lambda$, $I^h_\infty=\varinjlim_\lambda I^h_\lambda=\bigcup_\lambda\iota_\lambda(I^h_\lambda)$, and $\eta_\infty:A\to A^h_\infty$ the ring map with $\eta_\infty\circ\alpha_\lambda=\iota_\lambda\circ(A_\lambda\to A_\lambda^h)$ for all $\lambda$; then $(A^h_\infty,I^h_\infty)$ is the henselization of $(A,I)$: if $\eta:A\to A^h$ is the henselization of $(A,I)$ [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization], there is exactly one ring map $u:A^h_\infty\to A^h$ with $u\circ\eta_\infty=\eta$, it is an isomorphism, and $u(I^h_\infty)=IA^h$. In particular, if $(A,I)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], then for every $\lambda$ there is exactly one ring map $\beta_\lambda:A_\lambda^h\to A$ with $\beta_\lambda\circ(A_\lambda\to A_\lambda^h)=\alpha_\lambda$; it maps $I_\lambda^h$ into $I$, the $\beta_\lambda$ are compatible with the $\varphi^h_{\mu\lambda}$, and they induce an isomorphism $\varinjlim_\lambda A_\lambda^h\cong A$ under which $\varinjlim_\lambda I^h_\lambda$ corresponds to $I$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A04 (lemma-henselization-colimit, line 3181) and its proof (Categories, adjoint-exact; Lemma 0FWT filtered-colimits-henselian; 'details omitted'); the functoriality (1), the uniqueness of $\beta_\lambda$ and $A^h=A$ for henselian $(A,I)$ are the left-adjoint property of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization, line 2980: henselization is left adjoint to the inclusion of henselian pairs into pairs, the inclusion being fully faithful); used in this form in Fundamental Groups, proof of Lemma 0GS2 (pione.tex, General case: 'we see that $A=\colim A_i^h$')

proof.text: Functoriality: obtain a henselian colimit from pair_henselization. For any colimit representative in the hypotheses, the unique colimit isomorphism in Under carries the structural map and hence the extended ideal to the chosen representative. Transport HenselianRing by mapping the Jacobson radical and pulling back each monic polynomial and simple root along the ring equivalence, then mapping its lifted root forward. For each transition F.map f followed by the target structure map, henselization_universal_property gives a unique lift. Ideal.map_map and hJ give ideal preservation. Choose these lifts; uniqueness applied to the identity and composite proves the two functor laws.

proof.text: Colimit pair: set Jh i = (J i).map (eta.app i).hom. Naturality and Ideal.map_map prove transition maps preserve Jh. The preceding colimit-isomorphism argument makes each stage henselian. filteredColimit_henselianPair supplies the ideal K of colimit G, its union-of-images membership description, and henselianness. Transport K and henselianness to the arbitrary colimit cocone d via the unique colimit isomorphism. This gives Ih and its required membership description. Descend the cocone eta followed by d.iota to obtain etaInf. The descriptions hI and hIh show I.map etaInf is contained in Ih. Conversely, each stage ideal Jh maps into I.map etaInf, since J i maps into I at c.iota i and the etaInf square commutes. Taking stage representatives proves Ih = I.map etaInf.

proof.text: Universal property of the colimit henselization: for any henselian pair (A,L) and phi from c.pt with I.map phi contained in L, lift c.iota i followed by phi through each stage henselization using henselization_universal_property. Uniqueness, naturality of eta and the cocone equations give compatibility. Descend these lifted maps by hd to obtain b : d.pt -> A. Applying hc.hom_ext gives etaInf followed by b = phi. Any other such b agrees at each d.iota by uniqueness of the stage lift, and hd.hom_ext then gives global uniqueness. Specialize to a henselization zeta : c.pt -> A, whose extended ideal is henselian by pair_henselization and transport, to obtain the comparison map u and its required unique factorization.

proof.text: Inverse and ideals: since (d.pt,Ih) is henselian and etaInf carries I into Ih, henselization_universal_property for zeta gives v : A -> d.pt with zeta followed by v = etaInf. For every comparison u satisfying etaInf followed by u = zeta, uniqueness of the colimit universal property just constructed makes u followed by v the identity of d.pt; uniqueness of the henselization universal property makes v followed by u the identity of A. These identities directly prove injectivity and surjectivity of u.hom. Finally Ih = I.map etaInf and Ideal.map_map give Ih.map u = I.map zeta.

proof.text: Henselian specialization: when (c.pt,I) is henselian, specialize the universal property of step 3 to its identity map. This supplies the stage maps beta_i, their uniqueness and ideal inclusions, their compatibility, and their descended map b with etaInf followed by b the identity. Apply the same universal property to etaInf into the henselian colimit pair to see b followed by etaInf is the identity. Thus b is bijective. Mapping Ih = I.map etaInf along b yields Ih.map b = I.

lean.statement: theorem pairHenselization_colimit {Λ : Type u} [Preorder Λ] [IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty Λ] (F G : Λ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (η : F ⟶ G) (J : ∀ i : Λ, Ideal (F.obj i)) (hJ : ∀ {i j : Λ} (f : i ⟶ j), Ideal.map (F.map f).hom (J i) ≤ J j) (hG : ∀ i : Λ, ∃ c : Cocone (ObjectProperty.ι (fun C : Under (F.obj i) ↦ AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map C.hom) ∧ Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap ((J i).map C.hom.hom) C.hom.hom (Ideal.le_comap_map)))), Nonempty (IsColimit c) ∧ ∃ e : c.pt.right ≅ G.obj i, c.pt.hom ≫ e.hom = η.app i) (c : Cocone F) (hc : IsColimit c) (I : Ideal c.pt) (hI : ∀ x : c.pt, x ∈ I ↔ ∃ (i : Λ) (a : F.obj i), (c.ι.app i).hom a = x ∧ a ∈ J i) (d : Cocone G) (hd : IsColimit d) : ∃ Ih : Ideal d.pt, (∀ x : d.pt, x ∈ Ih ↔ ∃ (i : Λ) (a : G.obj i), (d.ι.app i).hom a = x ∧ a ∈ (J i).map (η.app i).hom) ∧ ∃ ηInf : c.pt ⟶ d.pt, (∀ i : Λ, c.ι.app i ≫ ηInf = η.app i ≫ d.ι.app i) ∧ (∀ (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (ζ : c.pt ⟶ A), (∃ ch : Cocone (ObjectProperty.ι (fun C : Under c.pt ↦ AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map C.hom) ∧ Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map C.hom.hom) C.hom.hom (Ideal.le_comap_map)))), Nonempty (IsColimit ch) ∧ ∃ e : ch.pt.right ≅ A, ch.pt.hom ≫ e.hom = ζ) → (∃! u : d.pt ⟶ A, ηInf ≫ u = ζ) ∧ (∀ u : d.pt ⟶ A, ηInf ≫ u = ζ → Function.Bijective u.hom ∧ Ideal.map u.hom Ih = I.map ζ.hom)) ∧ (HenselianRing c.pt I → ∃ β : ∀ i : Λ, G.obj i ⟶ c.pt, (∀ i : Λ, η.app i ≫ β i = c.ι.app i ∧ (∀ b : G.obj i ⟶ c.pt, η.app i ≫ b = c.ι.app i → b = β i) ∧ Ideal.map (β i).hom ((J i).map (η.app i).hom) ≤ I) ∧ (∀ {i j : Λ} (f : i ⟶ j), G.map f ≫ β j = β i) ∧ ∃ b : d.pt ⟶ c.pt, (∀ i : Λ, d.ι.app i ≫ b = β i) ∧ Function.Bijective b.hom ∧ Ideal.map b.hom Ih = I)
